title: DC-area forecast: Tranquil tonight. Sunday rounds of showers and downpours possible.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Partly to mostly cloudy this evening as temperatures fall back to near 80. Lows dip near 70 to mid-70s.

What's next? Sunday midday into Sunday night looks to be the wettest period through midweek, with storm chances lingering into Monday. Tuesday and Wednesday look mostly to fully dry, with some humidity relief.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Slowly increasing clouds. Maybe a couple showers or sprinkle near dawn. Somewhat humid as lows dip near 70 to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow (Sunday): Scattered showers are likely at times during the morning and afternoon. An occasional gusty downpour and thunder are possible, especially in the afternoon. Very humid as mostly cloudy skies limit highs to the mid-70s to near 80, perhaps low to mid-80s in a few spots that see more sun peeking through. A half-inch of rain broadly possible, with locally higher totals in downpours. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Showers and storms continue. The threat for a gusty thunderstorm should die down after 8 or 9 p.m. but the potential for flooding downpours may persist past midnight. Skies are mostly cloudy otherwise. Muggy lows near 70 to mid-70s. Another quarter to half inch of rain broadly possible, with locally higher totals in downpours. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Partly sunny on Monday with highs in the upper 80s and low 90s. It remains humid and a few lingering showers and storms are possible, mainly during the afternoon. Confidence: Medium

Tuesday is when we should start to see some gradual relief from the humidity. It's mostly sunny with highs in the mid-80s to near 90. Expect similar conditions on Wednesday. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: Pretty typical August conditions today. Mostly sunny with a touch of humidity, but overall a quiet summer day. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 15

A brutal 1988 heat wave peaked at a record 103 degrees before a violent thunderstorm swept through, knocking out power to tens of thousands and turning the sky dark with intense lightning and torrential rain.
